models_evaluated: 15 proprietary and open-source LLMs (individual models not named in the abstract)

links.outcome: Answer stability of previously correct MedQA responses under dynamic adversarial mutation of test cases
links.effect: 94% of previously correct answers failed dynamic robustness tests despite median MedQA accuracy above 80%; HealthBench failure rates exceeded 70% for top-tier models.
links.quote: Despite median MedQA accuracy exceeding 80%, 94% of previously correct answers failed our dynamic robustness tests.

links.outcome: Gap between static benchmark scores and dynamic reliability, including ranking shifts across evaluations
links.effect: Profound gap between high static benchmark performance and low dynamic reliability (the 'Benchmarking Gap'). Top models had failure rates over 70% on HealthBench, with stark ranking shifts.
links.quote: Applying DAS to 15 proprietary and open-source LLMs revealed a profound gap between high static benchmark performance and low dynamic reliability - the ''Benchmarking Gap''.

links.outcome: Ability of automated adversarial red-teaming agents to uncover LLM vulnerabilities, validated against clinicians
links.effect: Adversarial agents, validated against board-certified clinicians with high concordance, surfaced high failure rates: privacy leaks in 86% of scenarios, bias priming altering recommendations in 81%, hallucination rates above 74%.
links.quote: Validated against board-certified clinicians with high concordance, a suite of adversarial agents autonomously mutates clinical test cases to uncover vulnerabilities in real time.

unlisted_practices: Dynamic, automated adversarial mutation of test cases as a living alternative to static benchmarks for medical LLM safety evaluation

screen.reason: Empirical study developing and evaluating an automated dynamic adversarial red-teaming framework (DAS) using agents to continuously stress-test medical LLMs across robustness, privacy, bias, and hallucination prior to deployment.
